**The issue title is still incomplete.** It currently reads `[FEATURE]:` with no descriptive text after the colon. Please update the title to something like:

> `[FEATURE]: Re-add "Open in external editor" to the new TUI`

Thanks for updating the issue — it now looks great! The title is descriptive, the feature request template is properly filled out, and the description clearly explains the problem and what you'd like to see. The `needs:compliance` label has been removed.

A cleaner architectural approach requires a capability-aware routing mechanism:

1. Capability Tagging: Introduce explicit feature arrays within the model registry (e.g., `features = ["text", "vision", "video"]`). If the active engine matches the target asset capability, OpenCode should bypass standard text parsing and route the binary file directly to the provider's native File API.

2. Tool Interception: As an immediate workaround, the core `view_file` tool hook can be overridden locally. A wrapper script can evaluate the environment variable for the active model and the file extension on every turn—safely passing text to the standard OS reader, but intercepting binary media to stream it via the Google File API whenever Gemini is engaged.

Still reproduces on `opencode acp` (v1.15.12, current `dev`) and it's especially bad over ACP. Driving opencode from an external ACP client, a hard `opencode-go` weekly usage limit makes the turn hang with **zero frames to the client** until the client gives up.

**Wire capture** (external ACP client, model `opencode-go/kimi-k2.6`):

    → initialize            ✅
    → session/new           ✅
    → session/set_model     ✅  (opencode-go/kimi-k2.6)
    → session/prompt        … no response, ever
    (no session/update, no stopReason, no error — client killed after 120s)

Meanwhile opencode's own logfile shows the provider error that's being retried:

    statusCode: 429
    type:       GoUsageLimitError
    url:        https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions
    message:    "Weekly usage limit reached. Resets in 5hr 56min. To continue
                 using this model now, enable usage from your available balance:
                 https://opencode.ai/workspace/wrk_…/go"

**Why it's unbounded:** in `session/retry.ts`, `retryable()` returns a non-null object for `GoUsageLimitError` (the `responseBody.includes("GoUsageLimitError")` branch), and `delay()` reads `retry-after` (~21,360s here → ~5.9h, under the `RETRY_MAX_DELAY` ≈ 24.8-day cap). `policy()` builds a `Schedule` that only terminates when `retryable()` is falsy — so it sleeps ~6h, retries, gets the same 429, sleeps ~6h again, forever. Because `session/prompt` is synchronous, the ACP client sees nothing the whole time (the TUI at least renders the retry status; ACP clients have no equivalent).

Capping attempts (#26369) helps the general case, but for the **hard Go weekly/monthly limit** the `retry-after` is hours, so even a few attempts is hours of client-invisible silence. This class (`action.reason === "account_rate_limit"`) is arguably never worth retrying within a session and should fail fast instead — see also the closed #24013, which tried exactly that. The ACP-visibility half is tracked in #27779 / #26378.

Related failure mode worth folding in: when the underlying error is a **retryable one that never succeeds** (a hard `opencode-go` `GoUsageLimitError` 429), `prompt()` doesn't even return a bare `end_turn` — it never returns at all, because `SessionRetry.policy()` keeps sleeping on the multi-hour `retry-after` indefinitely (#21960). Over ACP that's total silence:

    → session/prompt   … no response, no session/update, no stopReason

So there are two layers here: once the retry loop is bounded (#21960 / #26369), this degrades into exactly the bare-`end_turn`-with-no-content symptom you describe — which means adding `throwOnError` / surfacing the assistant message's internal `error` is necessary for the failure to ever become visible to the client. Both fixes are needed; this issue is the one that makes the turn-level provider error protocol-visible.

PR #29061 implements this (`session.prompt(..., { throwOnError: true })`) and declares it Closes this issue — though note it currently surfaces the error as a text chunk and still returns `stopReason: "end_turn"`, and it only fires once the prompt RPC returns (which the unbounded retry in #21960 prevents for hard Go limits).

Thanks for capping this — it fixes the runaway transient case. One gap that echoes @niStee's comment above: for the **hard `GoUsageLimitError`** weekly/monthly Go limit, `delay()` returns the full `retry-after` (hours), so each of the 3 attempts sleeps for ~6h. Capped at 3 that's still ~18h of silence before the schedule gives up — and over ACP the `session/prompt` call is synchronous, so the client gets **zero frames** that entire time (repro + wire capture in #21960).

Suggestion: keep the attempt cap for transient 5xx / generic 429s, but treat the `account_rate_limit` class (`GoUsageLimitError`) as **non-retryable / fail-fast** in `retryable()` — since its `retry-after` is hours, retrying never helps within a session. That way it halts immediately and the failure can be surfaced (TUI already has the limit message; ACP needs #27779 / #29061 to make it protocol-visible). Happy to test a build against our ACP repro harness if useful.

The `throwOnError: true` + catch in `prompt()` is the right fix for the swallowed-error case (#27779) — nice. Two notes from testing this against a hard `opencode-go` quota limit:

**1. It still returns `stopReason: "end_turn"` on failure.** The catch surfaces the error as an `agent_message_chunk` (`Error: …`) and then returns `stopReason: "end_turn"`. So the text is visible, but a client that keys off `stopReason` to detect failure — which is exactly what #24494 asks for ("the client needs a protocol-visible failure, not end_turn") — still sees a normal end_turn. The PR description says `stopReason: "error"`, but the code path returns `end_turn`; worth reconciling so #24494 is fully closed.

**2. It's gated on the retry loop actually terminating.** For a hard `GoUsageLimitError` (429 weekly Go limit), `this.sdk.session.prompt()` never returns: `SessionRetry.policy()` sleeps on the multi-hour `retry-after` and retries forever (#21960), so the new catch is never reached and the ACP client still gets zero frames after `session/prompt`. Repro + wire capture in #21960. This PR plus a retry fail-fast for the `account_rate_limit` class (#21960 / #26369) together fully close the silent hang; neither does it alone.

Happy to run a build with both against our ACP wire-capture harness and report back.

I've pushed the local commits that resolve the silent slumber and network hang gaps we discussed:
1. `fix(opencode): abort retry slumber on hard quota limits or excessive delay` - Capped the slumber retry loop at 60 seconds.
2. `fix(core): inject 180s TTFB default timeout in ai-sdk fetch wrapper` - Added a hard timeout to prevent infinite network stalls.
3. `docs(spec): mark background-task-fallback-gap as resolved` - Updated the v2 spec to document these root-cause network fixes.

All fixes passed secret scanning locally and are actively preventing the gpt-5.5 network hangs in my live session right now. Ready for review!

Adding another data point from using OpenCode Desktop through the opencode harness.

Right now it is difficult to reliably tell which Git branch the active agent/session is running on without asking the agent or opening another session/window to inspect the context. That makes it too easy to lose track of whether work is happening on the intended branch or worktree.

This is important consistency information during agent-driven work. The current session UI should persistently show the active Git branch so users can verify at a glance that changes are being made in the expected context.

Follow-up: I've also pushed a commit to mirror the 180s TTFB timeout patch into the v1 `provider.ts` fetch wrapper (see https://github.com/niStee/opencode/commits/local-stable). This ensures that subagents using providers like `opencode-go` also benefit from the timeout and cleanly fallback instead of hanging indefinitely on stale connections.

Confirming this reproduces on the **Electron desktop app v1.15.13** (macOS, arm64) — not just the CLI. Your root-cause analysis (`message-v2.ts` stripping `providerMetadata` when `differentModel === true`) matches the symptom exactly.

**Trigger in my setup**:
- `opencode.json` declares `thinking` for `claude-opus-4-6-20250514`.
- The active session actually runs `claude-opus-4-8` (variant `max`, thinking `budgetTokens` 31999) — this is the on-wire `modelID` recorded in the message row.
- Config modelID ≠ wire modelID → the `differentModel` branch is taken → `providerMetadata` (carrying the signature) is dropped on every reasoning part on replay → Anthropic returns 400 on multi-turn.

**Persisted error from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/2026-05-31T210903.log`**:

```
ERROR service=session.processor session.id=ses_1802048ecffeR3QYgxUDXuFe9t
messageID=msg_e7fe5ad28001Oe2AhSzVeN4Z9l
error=messages.1.content.21: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the
latest assistant message cannot be modified.
  at /Applications/OpenCode.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/out/main/chunks/node-CiOkNpBx.js:197462
  at async postToApi (.../node-CiOkNpBx.js:197390)
  at async AnthropicMessagesLanguageModel.doStream (.../node-CiOkNpBx.js:347060)
```

**Anthropic response (verbatim, from the persisted error record in SQLite)**:

```
"statusCode": 400, "isRetryable": false
"request_id": "req_011CbbLmSxWcMmKJUfhaBTST"
"message": "messages.1.content.21: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in
 the latest assistant message cannot be modified. These blocks must remain as
 they were in the original response."
```

**Environment**:
- OpenCode.app **v1.15.13** (Electron, macOS arm64, `app.asar` 103 MB)
- Single plugin loaded: `@ex-machina/opencode-anthropic-auth@1.7.5` (audited: `transform.js` does not touch reasoning blocks — only `system` prompt and `tool_use` block `name`)
- Provider: Anthropic OAuth (Claude Pro/Max)
- Model: `claude-opus-4-8`, variant `max`, extended thinking enabled (31999 tokens)
- SQLite DB at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`: 850 sessions / 88,166 messages / 340,509 parts / 7.2 GB. Long-term users hit this fast.

**Hypothesis on a manual workaround** (not yet tested on my end — would appreciate confirmation): explicitly declare the on-wire model (`claude-opus-4-8` in my case) in `opencode.json` with its own variants block, so the config modelID matches the wire modelID and `differentModel` evaluates to `false`. Brittle — breaks the next time the wire model auto-bumps — so the proper fix you propose (preserve `providerMetadata` unconditionally on reasoning parts) is what we need.

Happy to provide more session/log detail if useful.

/set parameter num_ctx 65536
/save gemma4-31-ctx64k

rerun opencode

Hope this works for you !

Problem solved! I found an opencode.bak and renamed it. 

The error analysis (The JSON schema crash)
OpenCode uses extremely strict JSON schema validation for opencode.json (specified via the $schema line: "https://opencode.ai/config.json").

The trigger: This schema is programmed in such a way that it does not allow unknown additional fields (additionalProperties: false).
The Crash: When I added the "mcpServers" field next to "mcp", OpenCode's strict parser declared the entire file as invalid/corrupt.
The fallback: Instead of starting with a faulty configuration, OpenCode falls back to an empty default configuration in memory in the event of a validation error. This meant that all projects, sessions, agents and settings temporarily appeared to be “hidden”.
Hope we can get this capability to reduce barrier to transition from Github Copilot CLI or Claude Code to OpenCode

@NPPprojects the “externally handled” edit outcome is a useful distinction. It is neither allow nor reject; it is a separate audited decision/result state.

For permission systems, that matters because the built-in edit must not execute, but the agent still needs a truthful tool result. A possible decision/result split:

- decision: approval_required
- user action: externally_handled
- execution result: skipped_builtin_apply
- evidence: external handler id / diff hash / target file hash if available

That keeps manual-apply workflows honest without lying to the model that the built-in edit ran. We have been modeling similar decision/result separation in Agent_Sudo: https://github.com/Kisyntra/Agent_Sudo

Great points, @m13v — you're right that post-hoc hooks only narrate the loss rather than preventing it. Option A and B (my original proposal) would indeed just tell the agent "here's what survived the summarizer," which doesn't fix the regression.

Option C (`preserve_sections`) is the most structural of the three, and your suggestion to persist the full session + fork a branch is even cleaner long-term. But both require significant engine-level changes.

In the short-to-medium term, I think the most practical path is the one outlined in **#24993 (`experimental.session.pre-compact hook`)** — a hook that fires *before* compaction with full tool access. That way, plugins and agents can proactively persist what matters (session state, identity context, recent decisions, scratchpad content) before the summarizer runs. It doesn't prevent compaction from being lossy, but it shifts the responsibility from "recovering after the loss" to "preserving what's needed before the loss."

Combined with #20290 (re-announcing tools post-compaction), these two hooks would cover most of the practical pain points without requiring a full architectural overhaul of how compaction works.
